text.p: - Slovenian president Milan Kucan met ministers of the former government for the last time on Monday. The new ministers are due to take up their positions by Wednesday.
- The number of Italian tourists in Slovenia this year is expected to increase by 10 to 15 percent, representatives of the tourist promotion centre said.
- The number of unemployed in Slovenia in January rose by 1.5 percent to 126,316, the unemployment office reported.

- Slovenian petrol companies pushed for changes in the state's system for determining petrol prices. Companies demanded that prices should be adapted to movement of petrol prices on the world market and to the rate of the tolar.

- Slovenian Minister of Economic Activities Metod Dragonja will visit Moscow on March 24 talk about planned construction of a gas pipe-line through Slovenia from Russia. Slovenia's part of the investment is expected to amount to 720 million marks ($399 million).
- The two largest state owned banks Nova Ljubljanska Banka and Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor are expected to finish their reconstruction soon.

- Slovenia's weekly Mladina has been ordered to pay four million tolars ($25,974) in damages to a former commander of Slovenia's Army special brigade after he won a libel case against the paper. It is the highest sum ever paid out in a libel case in the history of Slovenia's justice system.
